creative.body:
I started keeping a constipation calendar 11 months into Wegovy. One green check for the days I went. A red X for the days I didn't. By month 6 the page was almost all red. My husband saw it on the fridge last week and started crying.

I have a paper planner I bought at Target three years ago. It used to be for grocery lists and grandkids' birthdays and the dates my husband's medication needed refills.

Last June, on a Tuesday morning at 6:47am, I sat down at the kitchen table with a green pen and a red pen and I started a different kind of calendar.

A constipation calendar.

One green check for every day I had a normal bowel movement. One red X for every day I didn't.

I am 64 years old. I have lost 47 pounds on Wegovy. I have a husband, three grandchildren, a 32-year teaching career, and a paper calendar in my kitchen drawer that has tracked my bathroom for 11 months.

I'd like to back up.

I went on Wegovy in February of last year. Not because I needed to lose weight to live longer. Because I had spent 41 years of my life thinking about food every 11 minutes and I had heard the word "silence" used in a Facebook group of women my age and I wanted to know if it was real.

It was real.

The first week the food noise stopped. I cried in my car at the Trader Joe's parking lot because I had not heard quiet inside my own head since 1983. I am not exaggerating. I do not have the energy to exaggerate.

The weight came off the way it comes off for women on the shot. 12 pounds the first 6 weeks. Another 14 in the next two months. I bought jeans I had not been able to button in 2009. I went to my niece's wedding in May and a woman I had not seen since high school said the words "you look like yourself again" and I went into the bathroom and I cried in a stall.

That is what the shot does. The shot fixes a thing nobody had been able to fix for me in 4 decades.

The shot also did something else.

The shot started slowing my stomach down.

The first month I noticed I was going to the bathroom every other day instead of every day. I thought maybe I needed more water. I drank more water. Nothing happened.

Month two I was going every third day, then every fourth. I started a Miralax in my morning coffee. Some days it worked. Most days it didn't.

Month three I added Metamucil. Then a magnesium. Then a probiotic the woman at the pharmacy promised would change my life. Then a fiber gummy. Then prune juice. Then Smooth Move tea. Then a senna at bedtime when nothing else worked.

By month five I was buying constipation products at three different stores so the cashiers wouldn't recognize me.

By month six I was spending close to $200 a month on bathroom products that did nothing.

By month seven I was sitting in my husband's recliner at 3am rocking back and forth because the brick in my stomach would not let me lie down.

That was the night I started the calendar.

I think I started the calendar because I had stopped trusting my own memory. People would ask me how I was feeling and I would say "fine" and I genuinely would not know if I had gone to the bathroom in the last 4 days or the last 9. The shame had blurred everything together into one long Tuesday.

Green check. Red X. I needed to see it on paper.

The first month of the calendar broke me.

I had assumed, somewhere in the back of my head, that I was being dramatic. That women complain about Wegovy constipation but really it can't be that bad. That if I was honest with myself I would see I had been going more than I remembered.

I tracked it for 30 days.

8 green checks. 22 red X's.

I stared at that page for a long time at my kitchen table. I made a cup of tea I did not drink. I called my daughter at 11pm and I told her about the calendar and she went very quiet on the other end of the line and then she said "Mom, I want you to take a picture of that and text it to me right now."

I texted it to her. She didn't text back for 6 minutes.

When she did, all she wrote was "I'll figure something out. Don't quit the shot."

She knows me. She knows what the shot has done for me. She knows I would rather sit in the recliner at 3am for the rest of my life than go back to 41 years of food noise.

She also knows what 22 red X's in a 30 day month means.

The second month of the calendar I started writing notes on the days I went red. I would put the X in the box and then I would write what I had tried that day in the margin.

"Doubled Miralax. No."

"Magnesium + senna. Cramps, no go."

"Metamucil 2x. Worse bloat."

"Prune juice. Nothing."

I started seeing a pattern that I had refused to see for 6 months when it was just blurry inside my head.

Nothing on my bathroom shelf was working.

Not "less" working. Not "sometimes" working. Not working.

When I added them up I had spent over $1,800 in 11 months on constipation products that produced 8 green checks and 22 red X's a month.

That is a worse return on investment than the slot machines in Atlantic City.

I am not normally a person who curses. I cursed at my kitchen table.

The week after I called my daughter, she sent me a video.

It was a doctor on Instagram, a gastroenterologist, talking to the camera about something I had never heard a doctor say before.

She said GLP-1 medication does not slow your colon. It slows your stomach. By up to 70% in some patients. She said the food sits there fermenting. She said that's where the gas and the sulfur burps come from. She said that's why the bloat is at the upper belly and not the lower belly.

And she said the laxatives I had been taking, every single one of them, work on the colon. The colon is six feet downstream of the stomach. Six feet.

She said I had been treating the wrong organ for 11 months.

I watched the video three times.

I made my husband come into the kitchen and I made him watch it.

He sat with me at the table. He looked at the calendar on the fridge with the 22 red X's. He looked at the bathroom shelf full of bottles. He looked back at the video.

He said, very quietly, "they have been pointing you at the wrong room."

That is the sentence the doctor had used in the video. He had not heard it from her. He had figured it out from the calendar.

I have been married to him for 41 years. I do not know that I have ever been more grateful for him than I was at my kitchen table that Tuesday afternoon.

I want you to picture your stomach as a kitchen sink.

Not a colon. Not "your gut." A kitchen sink with a drain at the bottom that empties into the rest of the plumbing.

When the drain works, you can rinse anything down. Coffee grounds, last night's pasta water, the scraps off the dinner plates. It all goes down. The sink stays clean.

GLP-1 medication does one thing extraordinarily well. It half-clogs the drain.

That is, in fact, the point of the medication. It slows your stomach so food sits there longer and you feel full longer and you eat less. The slowdown is the medication doing its job. That is why the shot works.

But here is what nobody told me at month one.

For about 79% of women over 50 on a GLP-1 longer than 12 months, that drain doesn't just slow. It half-clogs and stays half-clogged.

Picture a sink with a half-clogged drain.

The water doesn't go down. It pools.

You scrape another plate into the sink. The food bits don't rinse away. They float.

You scrape a second plate. A third. The pile builds.

The pile sits in standing water and starts to ferment. Anyone who has left dishes in a clogged sink for 48 hours in summer knows that smell. That sulfur. That rotten egg note.

That smell, coming up through the drain into the kitchen, is the same smell that crawls up my esophagus into my mouth at 2pm on a Thursday.

The sulfur burps. The brick in the stomach. The bloat. The food I ate Sunday still sitting there Wednesday. The 22 red X's on a paper calendar.

It is all the same thing.

It is a kitchen sink with a half-clogged drain.

The villain has a name. It is the slowed stomach.

And every single thing on my bathroom shelf, the Miralax, the Metamucil, the magnesium, the prune juice, the senna, the probiotics, every single one of them was pointed at my colon.

The colon is six feet under the floor on the other side of the house.

The clog is in the sink.

Pouring drain cleaner into the bathtub does nothing for a clog in the kitchen sink.

That, in one sentence, is why nothing has been working.

Not because my body is broken. Not because I am a difficult case. Not because I have "Wegovy gut."

Because every product I have reached for has been treating the wrong room.

My daughter is the one who actually found Motilli.

I want to be very honest about this because I do not want anyone reading this thinking I am sponsored or that I get paid every time someone clicks something. I have told my story so many times in the last 8 weeks at book club, at my hairdresser, at the grocery checkout, that my daughter said I should write it all down so I could just send it to people.

She found a small company called Motilli. They make a heart-shaped gummy. Two a day. The whole thing is built around three plant compounds I had never heard of in my life.

Apigenin from celery and chamomile. The compound that makes the stomach muscle remember how to contract on its own again.

Chlorophyll from mulberry leaf and alfalfa. The thing that binds the sulfur compounds in the stomach before they crawl up.

Apple pectin. A different kind of fiber than the bulking psyllium kind. This one softens the food bolus while it is still in the stomach so it actually moves down.

Wake the stomach. Clear the ferment. Move the chain.

All three of them aiming at the stomach. None of them at the colon.

Six feet up from where the laxatives have been pointing for 11 months.

I will be honest. I did not believe it the first day. I had been burned too many times. I had ordered too many "GLP-1 gut" products on Amazon that turned out to be Metamucil with a price markup.

I started the gummies on a Monday morning.

By Friday morning of that first week I had three green checks on my calendar in a row.

Three.

In a row.

I had not had three in a row since March of last year.

I sat on the edge of my bed that Friday morning with my hand over my mouth because I did not want to wake my husband up by crying.

I want to tell you what changed in the next 6 weeks because if I do not tell you the boring middle part you will not believe me about the rest.

Week 2 the sulfur burps stopped. Just stopped. I went 9 days without a single one. My husband and I went out to dinner Friday night and I laughed at something the waiter said and I did not panic. I had not laughed in public since November.

Week 3 the bloat dropped. I do not mean a little. I mean two pant sizes. Not from more weight loss. The shot had taken all the fat I was going to lose six months earlier. The pant sizes that came off were standing-water pant sizes. They came off because the kitchen sink finally drained.

Week 4 my husband told me my face looked less puffy. I had not realized my face had been puffy. I cried again. I have cried more in the last 6 weeks than I cried in the previous 20 years.

Week 6 I started forgetting to take the gummies. Not because I was being careless. Because my body had stopped reminding me with the brick at the dinner table.

That is when I knew.

The gummies were not papering over the problem. They had reset the stomach.

I went back to the calendar at the end of week 8. I counted the green checks. 51 out of 56 days.

51 green checks.

In two months.

I had gone from 8 green checks a month to 25 a month. From 22 red X's to 5.

I took the calendar off the fridge and I put it in the bottom drawer of my desk. I do not need to track the bathroom anymore.

That is what the upstream tool does, given the right room.

I am not a doctor and I am not telling you what to do with your body.

What I can tell you is what worked for me after the kitchen sink approach failed for 11 months.

If you are sitting at your own kitchen table right now with a calendar full of red X's and a bathroom shelf full of bottles you are too tired to throw away, I want you to know two things.

The first is that you are not crazy. The shame of this thing is louder than the thing itself. The calendar is not a sign you are losing it. The calendar is a sign you are paying attention. That is a different thing from losing it.

The second is that the products on your shelf were not designed for your problem. They were designed for a colon problem in 1985. Your stomach problem in 2026 needs an upstream tool. The colon products were never going to work. Not because of you. Because of the 6 feet of small intestine between the room they were treating and the room your food is actually stuck in.

The gummies are called Motilli. Two of them, the heart-shaped ones, every day. That is the entire protocol.

I want to walk you through the four reasons I am telling you to click the button below tonight instead of waiting until next week.

The first is the 90 day promise.

Motilli will refund you for any reason inside 90 days. You keep the bottle. There is no phone call to make. No form to fill out. No "we'll send a return label and reimburse you in 6 to 8 weeks." You email them, they refund the card, the bottle stays in your kitchen.

I want you to read that paragraph again because I have never in my life been offered that on a constipation product. Every other thing I bought in the 11 months I was tracking the calendar had a "no returns on opened bottles" sticker on the back of the box. Including the probiotic. Including the fiber blend my friend's chiropractor swore by.

Motilli is the only one that has said, in writing, that if the calendar does not start filling in green inside 90 days, the money goes back into your account.

So the question is not whether you can afford to try it. The question is whether you can afford to keep doing what you have been doing.

The second is something my daughter explained to me that I think you should know.

Motilli is a small company. The heart-shaped gummies are not made in a giant factory. They batch-produce them because the apigenin from the celery extract starts to lose strength once it sits on a shelf for too long. That is also why most celery extract products on Amazon do not work. They sit in a warehouse for 8 months before they get to you.

Motilli does not keep months of inventory sitting around. The trade-off is that they sell out for stretches at a time, especially as more women in our age bracket start finding them. The week I ordered, the page was within days of going dark.

If they are in stock when you click the button, that is the day to order. I am not saying that to push you. I am saying that because I do not want you sitting at your kitchen table next Wednesday looking at the back-in-stock notification page and counting another red X on the calendar that did not need to be a red X.

The third is the math my husband did at the table the night I started counting.

I had spent over $1,800 in 11 months on bottles that produced 8 green checks a month. That is roughly $225 for every green check.

I do not know what your bathroom shelf looks like right now. I will guess it looks something like mine did. Three Miralax bottles in different stages of empty. A magnesium that worked once. Two probiotics. A senna. A box of Smooth Move tea pushed to the back. Maybe a fiber gummy you stopped taking because it made the bloat worse.

Add up what is on that shelf. I will wait.

Whatever the number is, it is the receipt for a problem you did not have. You did not have a colon problem. You had an upstream problem nobody at the pharmacy ever named for you.

Every month you keep buying the wrong products is another month of that receipt.

The fourth is the part I almost did not say because I am 64 years old and I do not like to be dramatic.

Every month you keep doing this is a month of the calendar that does not have to be red.

I lost 11 months of my life to the bathroom shelf. I lost dinners with my husband. I lost a vacation we took in October that I spent half of in the hotel room. I lost the easy laugh I used to have at restaurants because I was always afraid of what was coming up next.

I do not get those 11 months back. You have not lost them yet.

Click the button below. The page will tell you the rest. Two of the heart-shaped gummies a day. Watch what the calendar does inside two weeks.

That is the only thing I am asking.

P.S. I want to say one more thing because I think it might be the most important thing in this letter.

If you have read this far, you already know.

You know the brick in the stomach at 9pm. You know the recliner at 3am. You know the bathroom shelf with the bottles you do not throw away because throwing them away would mean admitting they did not work. You know the calendar in the drawer that nobody is supposed to see.

You did not need a stranger on the internet to tell you any of that.

What you needed was someone to tell you that there was a different room. The right one. Six feet upstream of where everything you have been doing has been pointing.

There is. There is a gummy that aims at it. There is a 90 day promise that says you do not pay if the calendar does not turn green. There is a small company that batch-makes the thing because the active compound does not survive a warehouse.

The button is below. The page is in stock as of this morning. I do not know if it will work for you the way it worked for me. I do know that the calendar in the bottom drawer of my desk has not had a single red X added to it in 23 days.

I am 64 years old. I am writing this in the kitchen where I started the calendar. The page is in the drawer. I am going to leave it there. You do not have to keep yours on the fridge either.

Click the button. The page will do the rest.

I will not tell you again. I have told you enough.

The button is below.
creative.title: My constipation calendar said 22 red X's last month. I'm 11 months into Wegovy.
